interactions.author: Ajeet Verma
interactions.content:
This seems like a LlamaIndex–Ollama integration bug, that's why you don't get the error when you run it directly from the terminal using ollama command.

But, when using the Ollama from the llamaIndex integration, this error occurs perhaps because LlamaIndex tries loading the base "phi3" model during the metadata call (even though phi3:mini is mentioned). And this issue occurs for other models as well (for example, llama3.2)

A simple fix is to explicitly add a context_window and you'll no longer receieve the ResponseError.

from llama_index.llms.ollama import Ollama

llm = Ollama(
    model = "phi3:mini",
    temperature = 0.7,
    max_tokens = 100,
    context_window=8000,
)

response = llm.complete("Hello, how are you?")
print(response)

output:

I'm an AI developed by Microsoft and do not have feelings, but I'm here to help! How can I assist you today? If you need information or support on a variety of topics, feel free to ask.

interactions.author: QuenK
interactions.title: Symfony AI: How to add additional models for the LM Studio bridge?
interactions.content:
I’m working with Symfony AI and the LM Studio bridge to manage my language models locally.
My goal is to add custom models that are not included in Symfony’s default ModelCatalog.

My YAML configuration looks like this:

ai:
  platform:
    lmstudio:
      host_url: "http://127.0.0.1:1234"

  agent:
    test:
      platform: 'ai.platform.lmstudio'
      model: 'ministral-3-3b'
      tools: false

Even though the model is loaded in LM Studio, Symfony does not detect it.

I created a custom ModelCatalog:

<?php
namespace App\Service;

use Symfony\AI\Platform\Bridge\Generic\CompletionsModel;
use Symfony\AI\Platform\Capability;
use Symfony\AI\Platform\ModelCatalog\AbstractModelCatalog;

final class LMModelCatalog extends AbstractModelCatalog
{
    public function __construct()
    {
        $additionalModels = [
            'ministral-3-3b' => [
                'class' => CompletionsModel::class,
                'capabilities' => [
                    Capability::INPUT_MESSAGES,
                    Capability::OUTPUT_TEXT,
                    Capability::OUTPUT_STREAMING,
                ],
            ],
        ];

        parent::__construct($additionalModels);
    }
}

What I understood

  • The LM Studio ModelCatalog is hardcoded, and some models are not included by default.

  • The official documentation does not clearly explain how to extend the catalog.

  • It seems that we need to inject a custom ModelCatalog service instead of using YAML, but I haven’t found a recent concrete example.

My question

How can we add additional models for the LM Studio bridge in Symfony AI in a clean way compatible with the current bundle configuration?

  1. Can this be done via YAML, or only via services.yaml?

  2. If it is via services.yaml, what is the recommended snippet to declare custom models with their capabilities?

interactions.author: Olivier
interactions.content:
The feature doesn't seem to be documented indeed, set let's dig into the source that parses the configuration file (ai.yaml):

public function loadExtension(array $config, ContainerConfigurator $container, ContainerBuilder $builder): void
{
    $container->import('../config/services.php');

    foreach ($config['platform'] ?? [] as $type => $platform) {
        $this->processPlatformConfig($type, $platform, $builder);
    }

    // Process model configuration and pass to ModelCatalog services
    foreach ($config['model'] ?? [] as $platformName => $models) {
        $this->processModelConfig($platformName, $models, $builder);
    }

After reading the platform key, the model key is processed by processModelConfig() to add extra models:

/**
 * Process model configuration and pass it to ModelCatalog services.
 *
 * @param array<string, array{class: class-string, capabilities: list<Capability|string>}> $models
 */
private function processModelConfig(string $platformName, array $models, ContainerBuilder $builder): void
{
    $modelCatalogId = 'ai.platform.model_catalog.'.$platformName;

    // Handle special cases for platform name mapping
    if ('vertexai' === $platformName) {
        $modelCatalogId = 'ai.platform.model_catalog.vertexai.gemini';
    }

    if (!$builder->hasDefinition($modelCatalogId)) {
        return;
    }

    $additionalModels = [];
    foreach ($models as $modelName => $modelConfig) {
        $additionalModels[$modelName] = [
            'class' => $modelConfig['class'],
            'capabilities' => $modelConfig['capabilities'],
        ];
    }

    if ([] === $additionalModels) {
        return;
    }

    $definition = $builder->getDefinition($modelCatalogId);
    $definition->setArguments([$additionalModels]);
}

According to the code, your ai.yaml file should look something like this:

ai:
  platform:
    lmstudio:
      host_url: "http://127.0.0.1:1234"

  model:
    lmstudio:
      ministral-3-3b:
        class: 'Symfony\AI\Platform\Bridge\Generic\CompletionsModel'
        capabilities:
          - !php/const 'Symfony\AI\Platform\Capability::INPUT_MESSAGES'
          - !php/const 'Symfony\AI\Platform\Capability::OUTPUT_TEXT'
          - !php/const 'Symfony\AI\Platform\Capability::OUTPUT_STREAMING'

  agent:
    test:
      platform: 'ai.platform.lmstudio'
      model: 'ministral-3-3b'
      tools: false

Custom OllamaEmbeddingsProvider with the abstract class to extends AbstractEmbeddingsProvider class

<?php

namespace App\Neuron\Providers;

use GuzzleHttp\Client;
use GuzzleHttp\RequestOptions;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;
use NeuronAI\RAG\Embeddings\AbstractEmbeddingsProvider;

class FixedOllamaEmbeddingsProvider extends AbstractEmbeddingsProvider
{
    protected Client $client;

    public function __construct(
        protected string $model,
        protected string $url = 'http://localhost:11434/api',
        protected array $parameters = [],
    ) {
        $this->client = new Client([
            'base_uri' => trim($this->url, '/') . '/',
            'timeout' => 60,
        ]);
    }

    public function embedText(string $text): array
    {
        $response = $this->client->post('embeddings', [
            RequestOptions::JSON => [
                'model' => $this->model,
                'prompt' => $text,
                ...$this->parameters,
            ],
            RequestOptions::HTTP_ERRORS => true,
            'timeout' => 60,
            'connect_timeout' => 5,
        ])->getBody()->getContents();

        $response = json_decode($response, true);

        return $response['embedding'];
    }
}

interactions.author: Peter Pointer
interactions.content:
The AI you are referring to is the vibe-based coding using natural language. In this case the AI is a human speech interface for coding. It makes non-developers able to create programs/apps/games, which wasn't quite possible like that before. It democratizes creating programs. The same way the printing press made spreading ideas easier. That's generally a good thing.

If you're not letting it create full programs, it can still be nice as a human language interface to problem solving. It helps with analyzing code, refactoring, create or help plan new features. As a developer you still need to know if the code it produces is useful. Or prompt it to validate its own code and cross your fingers.

In all cases you will need to set up tests that prove your program does what you want it to and keep updating the tests as you go along. The job hasn't changed there.

Of course companies could replace their software developers if that gets sophisticated enough. They could also be smart and multiply the use of each developer, instead of handing them over to the competition.

When AI goes wrong it is very annoying to talk to this all-knowing 8-year old, which understandably is very frustrating in a way that betrays the AI's premise - makes me want to go back to keywords and syntax. So now we have to use speech in a certain way instead of using our natural language. Almost like a programming language of its own.

Humanity will also need to produce more code to train AI on. I suspect it will become more of an ecosystem of traditional developers together with AI-based developers. It's just currently shifting where each company wants to position itself.

MicroSoft made a nice set of presentations about using AI. It's free on GitHub:
https://github.com/microsoft/generative-ai-for-beginners
